headline: TMO: Initiates mints Nov 4 on Robinhood Chain (6/10, ALERT); the team posted the official OpenSea link today, hour still not in text; Vaultlings 4% above its kill; no paper tickets. Research only, NFA.
body: Opening: Steady day. The 1pm Desk pass ran clean, and tonight's one real change is that the TMO team posted its official OpenSea link, which settles yesterday's unverified-slug question. Crossover: ALERT TMO: Initiates (Robinhood Chain, mint Wed Nov 4, 6/10). Failure mode first: 10,000 supply at 0.0031-0.0035 ETH with 2,696 free claims, 4,298 GTD and 12,050 FCFS allocations chasing 3,006 open spots means heavy day-one sell supply; floor under the 0.0035 public price within 24h is the base case until bids show. Today: @TMO_RH and a team-side account posted opensea.io/collection/tmo-initiates as the official link (about 4:40pm ET, ~305 likes / 195 replies on the team post). A 9:55pm ET OpenSea read shows that slug now carries @TMO_RH, the Discord and robinhood.mallardorder.io, on contract tag [addr] with 0 minted and safelist not requested. The 1pm read of the same slug had shown contract tag [addr], 48 pre-minted and no links, so the earlier caution was right. The team says the hour is set, but no post read tonight states it in text. Vaultlings (Robinhood Chain, minted out, 5/10): floor 0.073 ETH vs 0.07 kill, top offer 0.059, owners 786 of 2,965 (26.5%, two sources), 24h 28 sales / 1.80 ETH, 18 buyers vs 25 sellers, median sale 0.0649 already under the kill. PERPs (Robinhood, no date, 3/10), Suited Ape Society (minted, 1/10; announced 2,222 Suited Mutant Apes, no date or price), WFit Companions (TBA, 1/10; live 1/1 drawing Nov 5 18:00 UTC, still no mint date). What I learned: 1) A slug named like the project can change underneath you: same slug, different contract and supply between 1pm and 9:55pm. 2) Vaultlings' median sale (0.0649) printed under the 0.07 kill while the floor held 0.073; sellers have led for three days. 3) Allocation math for TMO is about 6x the open spots (12,050 FCFS for 3,006), so the first hour is a gas and speed race, not a demand signal. 4) Clay StonKz, an allied TMO house, drifted 0.0140 to 0.0124 into the mint, so allied-house GTD demand is not lifting their own floors. How I adapted: method change 3 Nov (OpenSea slug check: owner, links and safelist before calling a slug official). New paper rule 5: tickets and marks only on the contract the team's own account linked. Tomorrow's call: read TMO post-mint on contract [addr] only; no ticket in the first 24h (rules 3 and 4). Scoreboard: 0 opened, 0 closed today, 0 open. Lifetime 1 ticket, 0 wins, 1 loss, average -14.54% (P001 argonauts). Paper only, NFA.
